I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. I checked the method by running the same script on Q2, and it reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a | segment `enterprise`, net sales 304,490,389 |
| b | 249 customers |
| c | category `sw`, net sales 277,337,347 |
| d | 2025-07 |
| e | u144@ex.com |
| f | 239 customers |
| g | 676,066 |
| h | -0.2% (August → September) |

The data had three problems I had to work around to match Q2:

- **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (ending in `Z`). I converted it to Korean time (+9 hours) before splitting by quarter and month. Orders are clustered right at month ends (e.g. 09-30 15:30Z, which is 10-01 in Korean time), and Q2 only matches after the conversion.
- **Segment spelling:** values like ` consumer`, `Enterprise ` and `SMB` have stray spaces and mixed case. I trimmed and lowercased them, so the answers use lowercase names.
- **Duplicate customers:** some emails appear under more than one customer ID, and the copies can have different segments. For b and f I counted one customer per email. Counting by ID gives 280 and 202 for Q2 instead of 236 and 181. Segment (a) uses the segment on the customer record each order belongs to.

STATUS: DONE
